# Four compatible roofs and a three-signature functional obstruction

This note continues the actual polygon geometry in
`candidate b85e6bd6eff40d13`.
Its first result is a family of actual compatible polygon variations.
Its second result is an exact obstruction to a proposed deduction from
face-incidence data and middle-face tent positivity. The obstruction is
NOT asserted to realize the prescribed section weights or genuine mixed
criticality. It is not a counterexample to (OC).

The general use of concave roofs and their convex-order dual is already
proved in `candidate ffc34ddb869ec7d5`.
The new tests here concern the restricted planar three-signature data,
the actual coupled-face roof family, and its explicit small inner face.

## 1. A two-parameter family of actual compatible roofs

Retain every hypothesis and notation of Sections 1--5 of the companion
source. In particular A,K,B are polygons, their support values agree in
the outward unit normal n, and

    F_K=[a,b], I_0=(F_A+F_B)/2=[a_0,b_0],
    J=(p+F_B)/2=[c,d],
    a<=a_0<c<=d<b_0<=b.

Coordinates are tangential arclength s and signed normal height t above
F_K. Choose any

    q_L in [a,a_0], q_R in [b_0,b].

After the actual A enlargement A_e=conv(A,p+e n), replace the old K
facet t<=0 by the three inequalities

    t<=e/2,
    t<=(e/2)(s-q_L)/(c-q_L),
    t<=(e/2)(q_R-s)/(q_R-d).                         (1)

Keep every other K facet. This gives an actual compatible polygon
K_e(q_L,q_R) for all sufficiently small positive e. Indeed its signed
roof

    G_(q_L,q_R)(s)
       =min{1,(s-q_L)/(c-q_L),(q_R-s)/(q_R-d)}         (2)

is nonnegative on I_0 and is one on J. The old Minkowski polygon
(A+B)/2 has exposed face exactly I_0; its other finitely many vertices
have a fixed negative limiting t-coordinate. Similarly the new seed
(p+e n+B)/2 has top face J at height e/2, and all its remaining vertices
have fixed negative limiting t-coordinates. They therefore satisfy (1)
for small e. The unchanged K facets are satisfied by the strict-support
argument in the companion source. Convexity proves containment of the
whole new midpoint body.

The same finite polygon argument proves boundedness, convergence to K,
and the O(e^2) corner remainder. Thus its middle normalized first-order
cost is exactly

    C_K(q_L,q_R)=(1/2) integral_a^b G_(q_L,q_R)(s) f(s) ds,
    f=W_K-r.                                        (3)

The A cost C_A is independent of these two choices. All source and
endpoint ownership conditions in the companion source still apply.

## 2. Four roofs suffice within this family

For any integrable real f, the minimum of (3) over the displayed
rectangle of parameters is attained at one of its four corners:

    (q_L,q_R) in {a,a_0} x {b_0,b}.                 (4)

Here the full-hull and fully trimmed roofs are two of the corners;
the other two trim only one side. To prove the assertion, the middle
plateau contributes the fixed integral over [c,d]. The left part is

    I_L(q)=[integral_a^c s f(s) ds
                    -q integral_a^c f(s) ds]/(c-q).

Its derivative has constant sign on [a,a_0]:

    I_L'(q)=integral_a^c (s-c)f(s) ds/(c-q)^2.         (5)

The right part is

    I_R(q)=[q integral_d^b f(s) ds
                       -integral_d^b s f(s) ds]/(q-d),

and likewise

    I_R'(q)=integral_d^b (s-d)f(s) ds/(q-d)^2.         (6)

Both denominators are strictly positive throughout their compact
parameter intervals. Each function is monotone or constant, so each
attains a minimum at an endpoint independently of the other. This
proves (4), including zero-derivative and point-plateau cases.

This minimizes the MENU COST within this family. It does not optimize
the total-mass derivative simultaneously and does not remove a tied
endpoint. The same chosen roof must satisfy the ownership conditions.

## 3. Exact obstruction with the permitted signature order

Normalize the face parameter to s in [0,1]. Choose weights and the
comparison ratio

    p_1=p_2=7/50, p_3=18/25, r=21/100.

They satisfy sum p_i=1, max p_i=18/25<3/4, every pair sum at least
7/25>1/4, and r<2/9. Let

    L=2579/10200, Z=7781/10200, c=9/10,
    A_*=7/100.

The three successive signatures on the face are

    {2} on [0,L), {1,2} on (L,Z), {1} on (Z,1].

Their cost density is exactly

    f(s)= -A_* outside [L,Z],
           A_* inside [L,Z].                         (7)

Values at the two breakpoints have no effect on any integral. Direct
integration gives

    m=integral_0^1 f(s) ds=7/5000,
    integral_0^1 s f(s) ds=63/50000=m c.              (8)

For clarity, Z-L=51/100 and Z+L=259/255. These imply (8)
without any numerical approximation. Also Z<c<1.

For EVERY finite concave function G on [0,1],

    integral_0^1 G(s) f(s) ds >= m G(c).              (9)

Here is a direct proof, with no numerical convex-order inference. The
signed measure

    nu=f(s) ds-m delta_c

has zero total mass and zero first moment by (8). It is nonnegative
on (L,Z), and nonpositive outside [L,Z]; the additional negative atom
is outside because c>Z. Let ell be the affine line interpolating
G(L),G(Z). Concavity gives G-ell>=0 on [L,Z] and G-ell<=0
outside [L,Z]. Therefore (G-ell)nu is a nonnegative measure, and

    integral G dnu=integral (G-ell) dnu>=0.

This is (9).

In particular every ordinary unit-height full-face tent T_t, t in
(0,1), has STRICTLY POSITIVE cost, since T_t(c)>0:

    integral T_t f >= m T_t(c)>0.                   (10)

Thus the necessary middle-only tent inequalities all hold, and the
signature order and weight bounds are the actual permitted ones.

Now set

    I_0=[899/1000,901/1000], J={c}.

Suppose the A face that maps to this I_0 has the low singleton
signature {1} throughout. In face-parameter units the A face has
twice the length of I_0, so its unit-height tent cost is

    C_A= -A_* |I_0| = -7/50000.                     (11)

For any finite concave middle displacement profile G whose new seed
has height one at c, compatibility requires G(c)>=1. Equation (9)
then proves

    C_A+(1/2) integral G f
       >= -7/50000+7/10000=7/12500>0.               (12)

This includes every roof (2), every parallel facet movement, and
every inclined affine roof; it is stronger than a four-corner check.
The constant affine roof G=1 gives equality in (9), so the lower
bound over this unconstrained concave-roof class is attained exactly.

An inner tent supported on I_0 has negative cost, and C_A<0, yet
middle tent positivity plus these three signatures does NOT force a
favorable coupled middle roof. The obstruction concerns this precise
functional implication; it does not assert a genuine critical body.

The obstruction also persists when the A apex is allowed to move
ANYWHERE in the relative interior of this same A face. Let its
midpoint position be c' in int I_0. The cost C_A remains (11),
because the A signature is constant on the whole face. Any compatible
concave roof has G>=0 on I_0 and G(c')>=1. Since c is the midpoint
of I_0, concavity between c' and the endpoint on the other side of c
gives G(c)>=alpha(c'), where

    alpha(c')=(c-a_0)/(c'-a_0) if c'>=c,
    alpha(c')=(b_0-c)/(b_0-c') if c'<=c,
    a_0=899/1000, b_0=901/1000.

Thus alpha(c')>1/2, and (9) implies the strict uniform bound

    C_A+(1/2) integral G f
       > -7/50000+7/20000=21/100000>0.              (13)

This infimum is exact: the affine roof through (a_0,0),(c',1)
for c'>=c, or through (b_0,0),(c',1) for c'<=c, realizes
G(c)=alpha(c') and equality in (9). Sending c' to the nearer
endpoint gives alpha tending to 1/2. Such affine roofs are actual
compatible polygon variations by the same finite-vertex proof as
Section 1: they are nonnegative on I_0 and reach the seed height.
For each fixed interior c', the remaining vertices retain their
strict limiting support slack. No limiting endpoint path is needed
for the positive lower bound (13).

Even a K-only signed concave variation constrained merely by
G>=0 on I_0 has nonnegative cost here, since G(c)>=0 and (9)
applies. Thus the functional obstruction respects more than the
outward-tent inequalities; it respects every such compatible signed
middle-face first-order cost as well.

## 4. The line incidence and shared face are geometrically realizable

The following exact construction checks that the three-line signature
order and tiny Minkowski face are not fictitious incidence data.
It deliberately does NOT claim the chosen p_i are its actual section
weights or that any displayed mixed cap is globally critical.

Take canonical normals v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1),v_3=(-1,-1), source 0,
and T={x<=1,y<=1,x+y>=-1}. Define

    X(s)=(s-L,Z-s), 0<=s<=1,
    F_K=X([0,1]), P=(-4/5,4/5),
    F_A={2X(s)-P: s in I_0}.

The three middle halfspaces are v_i x>=0. Along F_K their signatures
are exactly those in Section 3: the first switches on at L, the
second switches off at Z, and v_3 X(s)=-(Z-L)<0 throughout.

Let B be the convex hull of

    P, (-11/10,1), (-6/5,1), (-3/5,-2/5),
       (-2/5,-3/5), (1,-6/5), (1,-11/10).

Every listed point lies in T. All three support values h_B(v_i)
equal 1, with positive-length exposed segments. Its exposed face in
direction (1,1) is the singleton P: P has sum zero and every other
listed point has strictly negative sum. The body is two dimensional.

Let A be the convex hull of F_A and the two points

    (-11/10,3/2), (-11/10,-11/10).

Its exposed face in direction (1,1) is exactly F_A, where x+y=51/50.
Both other vertices have smaller coordinate sum. All three cuts
v_i x=-1 meet int A: the x coordinates occur on both sides of -1,
the y coordinates occur on both sides of -1, and coordinate sums
occur on both sides of 1. On F_A itself the signature is exactly
{1}, with strict inequalities. For example y<-1 and x+y=51/50>1
throughout its small parameter interval, while x>-1.

Finally set

    K=conv(F_K union (A+B)/2 union [-1/10,1/10]^2).

It is a polygon with source 0 in its interior and contains the
actual midpoint body. Its exposed face in direction (1,1) is exactly
F_K: the midpoint body's face is X(I_0), and the small square has
strictly smaller support. Thus all middle cuts are proper and the
shared-face geometry is exactly the one used above.

Tangential arclength on F_K is sqrt(2) ds, and on F_A it is
2 sqrt(2) ds. Consequently the actual arclength costs in (11)--(12)
are multiplied by the same positive factor sqrt(2). All signs and
ratios are unchanged.

The additional relations imposed by genuine depth criticality and
the ACTUAL values of sigma_A,sigma_K are not verified by this
construction. The conclusion is therefore precisely that the
listed incidence, numerical gauge bounds, face geometry, and all
middle-only tent inequalities do not ALONE imply a favorable
concave shared-face repair. A further relation from actual sections,
global source competition, or the B contraction cost is required.

## 5. One omitted actual-section constraint, with an exact area charge

The preceding distinction between assigned weights and actual critical
weights is substantive. Here is an explicit additional constraint that
the numerical profile does not test. Assume now the ACTUAL planar
critical-cut hypotheses of
`candidate 86934b651b11f7d5`.
For this section only, write

    a_i=sigma_Ai, k_i=sigma_Ki, s_i=k_i+2a_i,
    lambda_i=1/s_i, Lambda=sum lambda_i,
    p_i=lambda_i/Lambda, t_i=a_i/s_i.

The proved chord-moment bound gives k_i>=a_i, so 0<t_i<=1/3.
For the symmetric actual core D=(K-y_0) intersect -(K-y_0), let
N be its gauge and let J denote a quarter turn. Retaining the exact
inequalities from that proof, rather than only their factor-three
consequence, gives

    2lambda_i/(1-2t_i) <= N(Jv_i)
       <= 2lambda_i/(1-4t_i+6t_i^2).               (14)

Indeed the nearer endpoint of the actual K chord has distance
rho_i in the normalized Jv_i parameter, with

    s_i(1-4t_i+6t_i^2)/2 <=rho_i<=s_i(1-2t_i)/2.

Taking reciprocals proves (14). The norm triangle inequality and
sum v_i=0 consequently imply, for distinct i,j,l,

    p_l/(1-2t_l)
       <=p_i/(1-4t_i+6t_i^2)
                        +p_j/(1-4t_j+6t_j^2).     (15)

This is an actual critical-section inequality; it is not asserted
for the explicit compatible polygons of Section 4.

In particular, if p_l>p_i+3p_j, then

    t_i >= [2-sqrt(6p_i/(p_l-3p_j)-2)]/6.          (16)

To check it, 1-4t+6t^2 decreases from 1 to 1/3 on [0,1/3].
Drop the factor 1/(1-2t_l)>=1 on the left of (15), and bound
the j-th term by 3p_j. The remaining inequality is
1-4t_i+6t_i^2 <=p_i/(p_l-3p_j)<1, whose lower root is (16).
The argument also proves p_l-3p_j<=3p_i, so the square root is
real. The symmetric assertion holds with i and j interchanged.

There is a simple whole-A area constraint on these section sizes.
For any two independent planar normals,

    |A| >= (1/2)|det(v_i,v_j)| sigma_Ai sigma_Aj.   (17)

To prove it, use coordinates (v_i.x,v_j.x). They scale area by
D_ij=|det(v_i,v_j)|. The two cut chords become respectively
vertical and horizontal segments of lengths D_ij sigma_Ai and
D_ij sigma_Aj. The convex hull of a horizontal segment of length
L and any vertical segment of length H has area at least LH/2:
if the vertical segment crosses the horizontal line, the two
triangles based on the horizontal segment have disjoint interiors
and total area LH/2; if it lies on one side, its farther endpoint
is at distance at least H and the single resulting triangle has
area at least LH/2. Their convex hull is contained in the transformed
A. Undoing its area factor proves (17), including endpoint contact.

For the canonical determinant-one normals and the assigned weights
p_1=p_2=7/50,p_3=18/25, (16) forces BOTH

    t_1,t_2 >= (1-1/sqrt(5))/3.

Equations (17) and a_i=t_i/(p_i Lambda) then force

    |A| Lambda^2 >= (1500-500sqrt(5))/441.          (18)

No upper bound relating Q Lambda^2 to the other data is proved here.
Thus (18) neither invalidates the scoped functional obstruction nor
turns it into an actual critical example. It records exactly one
additional common-body constraint that any realization must satisfy.
